summary.headline: Shakti Pumps Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 858 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to about 10% in the quarter and FY26 margin was about 16%.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a transition year balancing growth with balance sheet discipline. Record FY26 consolidated revenue of INR 2,698 crore and Q4 revenue of INR 858 crore were driven by solar pump installations of 86,086 in FY26 (up 20%) and 28,345 in Q4 (up 51%). Receivables fell by over INR 420 crore in Q4 to INR 1,276 crore, with FY26 operating cash flow of INR 124 crore. Margin pressure from raw material inflation, Magel Tyala realisation cuts and freight costs persisted, and management gave no numerical margin or FY27 revenue guidance.

financial_highlights.change: Down from INR 1,697 crore at 31 Dec 2025; receivable days improved by 77
Management says FY26 full-year rate about 27%

segments.name: Solar pumping (core)
segments.commentary: Q4 solar execution about INR 704 crore against FY26 about INR 2,080 crore; installations up 51% YoY in Q4. Margin compressed by raw material inflation and Magel Tyala realisation cuts of 3-4%.

segments.name: Solar rooftop (Shakti Energy Solutions)
segments.commentary: Early stage; inverters placed in market for trials, with customer feedback of about 10% better generation. Management guides EBITDA margin of about 15% for this business, with no revenue numbers given.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Stable FY26 but Q4 hit by order placement delays amid Middle East tensions. Management says export margin is about 10% higher than domestic; exports go to 100+ countries.

segments.name: EV motors and controllers
segments.commentary: Still in emerging stage; about INR 70 crore of INR 114 crore capex invested. Management expects results in the next 6-12 months, with vehicle-level trials under way.

guidance_outlook: Order book about INR 1,500 crore as of 7 May 2026, which management expects to execute over the next two quarters.
Management expects margins to improve as raw material costs (copper, stainless steel, silicon sheets) normalise, but gave no number; it will update in Q1 FY27.
Expanded pump capacity and 0.5 GW module capacity from Q2 FY27 (module plant to be commissioned by end Q1 FY27); 2.2 GW solar cell capacity targeted by March 2028.
KUSUM 2.0 expected to roll out by end Q1 FY27, with orders from Q2 FY27 onward per management.
No numerical FY27 revenue or installation guidance; management reiterated year-on-year growth intent.
capex_capacity: Expanded solar pump capacity expected from Q2 FY27.
0.5 GW solar module plant expected to be commissioned by end Q1 FY27; in-house panel production to support margins.
2.2 GW solar cell capacity targeted by March 2028.
EV business capex about INR 70 crore spent out of INR 114 crore total.
demand_pricing: Competition has increased, pressuring L1 tender prices; Magel Tyala recent tenders cut realisation by 3-4%.
Maharashtra: about INR 500-524 crore of the order book; Maharashtra execution was slowed in Q3 on payment delays and resumed after payment clarity.
Operating leverage benefit of about 2-3% offset by raw material impact of about 6-7% in Q4, per management.
Export margin about 10% higher than domestic per CFO.
Management said it will report Q1 FY27 margin update; it declined to give order-level margins or tender pricing approach.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins return to the 24% peak seen in H1 FY26 and FY25?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed raw material inflation (copper, stainless steel, silicon sheets) and a stronger USD; CFO called it temporary but declined to give a target, saying an update will come in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Maharashtra payment issue resolved and why are receivables still rising?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said receivables fell in Q4 and INR 916 crore of INR 1,276 crore is not yet due; payments are tied to RMS data (90% after 7 days, 10% after 90 days), and the Maharashtra dues problem is resolved.

qa_highlights.question: Is margin being factored into bids, given order book margin of about 11% per one analyst?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margins on the current order book are at the same level as stated; tender pricing varies by state and competition, and the company will update on margins each quarter. Chairman declined to discuss bid rates.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Q4 tax rate of about 42% persist?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the spike reflects year-end provisions (warranty, dividend tax, CSR) on lower profit; the full-year rate is about 27%, which is normal.

qa_highlights.question: Timing of KUSUM 2.0 and whether FY27 revenue will exceed INR 3,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects KUSUM 2.0 to roll out by end Q1 FY27 with orders from Q2 FY27; it gave no FY27 revenue number.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q1 FY27 bookings be recognised within 90-120 days given the KUSUM extension?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said execution timelines were extended by the government for all players, so recognition timing moves out; he asked analysts to rely on the order book figures.

risks_watch: Margin recovery depends on raw material normalisation; Q4 EBITDA margin was about 10% against about 16% for FY26.
Receivables of INR 1,276 crore (about 120-150 days historically); collection from state RMS data is the key cash risk.
KUSUM 2.0 timing has slipped; delivery depends on government notification and state tenders.
Order book disclosed as of 7 May 2026 with GST included, which analysts said makes quarter-on-quarter comparison hard; management agreed to show ex-GST values going forward.
Export recovery uncertain amid Middle East disruption.
KUSUM 1 payment status not disclosed; management will share separately.
Q4 effective tax rate of about 42% to be watched in Q1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and balance sheet repair, but evasive on margins, FY27 revenue and tender pricing, repeatedly deferring numbers to Q1 FY27 updates. Management attributes margin pressure to temporary geopolitical and raw material factors.
key_quotes: Importantly, these are external and cyclical headwinds, not a structural issue.
Receivables were reduced by over INR 420 crores during the fourth quarter, reduced from INR 1,697 crores as of December 31st, 2025, to INR 1,276 crores as of March 31st, 2026.
We are not guiding on any number at the moment. We are saying that we will continue to grow.
So, this is just a temporary impact because of the geopolitical situation and other things.

adds.what: Expanded solar pump capacity (unquantified) from Q2 FY27
2.2 GW solar cell capacity by March 2028

growth.why: No numeric FY27 revenue guidance; management reiterates YoY growth intent, backed by a INR 1,500 crore order book to execute over two quarters, 0.5 GW module plant by end Q1 FY27 and expanded pump capacity from Q2 FY27, with 2.2 GW cell capacity targeted only by March 2028.
